findings: EXACTNESS DEPENDS ON IN-ORDER RETURNS: with the controller model of record (RW 16, FR-FCFS reorder window, as every other bench uses) the PS segments mis-assemble rows: a later read's beats land in an earlier row's buffer (slot 0 of rq 0 carries sector 4), rows go out with smask 0111; SW production run 49,420 of 65,472 rows, 16,053 errors (FAIL). The PS group unit (ot_svs_grp, 2 row buffers a PC) assumes per-PC in-order beats (the bench stub returns in order). Either the die controller must guarantee per-PC in-order returns, or ot_svs_grp needs a tag-indexed row buffer (KNO 15 = up to 15 rows outstanding a PC).

RATE: in-order, no-credit: 0.786-0.831 of stack peak (worst over 5 refresh phases, end-to-end incl. first access; steady 0.792-0.838); credited: 0.726-0.741. vs the simulator's 0.950 stream term -> ratio 1.208 worst / 1.176 mean (UNQUALIFIED); vs the gu record requirement 0.775 -> 0.986 no-credit / 1.067 credited (the token price holds, gu stays SM-bound).

7 of the 17 elements' adopted closures are LEGACY seg routes without per-PC streams (hfd_svc_SE_s0..s3, hfd_svc_SW_s0/s1/s5: best = tt_c10b5fc9a / tc_4aadc92bc jobs; every PS route of these is CANCELLED / EARLY_FAIL); the bench qualifies the PS RTL these segments must close in.
notes: One bench per family represents every slice: the 17 elements are the x-segments of the SE (s0..s8, NE family) and SW (s0..s7) stream-service chains; a stream passes through every segment of its family, so each family's composed run measures all its slices; SW and NE (SE segments) agree to <= 0.006.
